variants.name: Thymeleaf natural templates (Spring Boot)
variants.implementation_notes: Thymeleaf is the Spring Boot default: the template is valid HTML that also opens in a browser, markers are attributes (th:text="${order.total}", th:each="row : ${rows}") and escaping is on unless th:utext is used. Templates live under src/main/resources/templates and are resolved by the SpringTemplateEngine; th:fragment/th:insert (or a layout dialect) supply the chrome, and Spring Boot exposes the cache switch for development.
variants.idiom_name: Thymeleaf templates with th:text/th:each resolved by SpringTemplateEngine
pitfalls: th:utext and th:inline="javascript" skip escaping and are the usual XSS entry point; reserve them for values assembled server-side.
Spring Boot caches parsed templates: set spring.thymeleaf.cache=false while developing or an edit appears not to take effect.
Expression errors surface as a 500 at render time - there is no compile-time proof that the template's ${...} paths exist on the model.

variants.name: Jakarta Server Pages with JSTL and EL
variants.implementation_notes: In a Jakarta EE servlet container the classic realization is still JSP: the container compiles each .jsp into a servlet, JSTL tags (<c:forEach>, <c:if>) plus the Expression Language (${row.name}) keep the page free of Java code, and layout is done with <jsp:include> or tag files. Choose it for existing servlet/Jakarta EE codebases; scriptlets (<% %>) bypass the model discipline entirely and should not appear in new pages.
variants.idiom_name: JSP page with JSTL tags and EL expressions
variants.code_sketch:
<%@ taglib prefix="c" uri="jakarta.tags.core" %>

  • -
pitfalls: EL output is not escaped in every configuration, so dynamic values in HTML should go through <c:out> (or an escaping function) instead of a bare ${...}.
Scriptlets put Java back into the page and destroy the separation the pattern exists for; enforce tag-only pages in review.
JSPs are compiled on first request unless a precompilation plugin is wired into the build, so a syntax error appears in the container log rather than at build time.
